issue_context.title: Netgear needs v2 login
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
Some Netgear routers seems to only accept v2 login and pynetgear therefore needs --login-v2 argument. Could Netgear component have this as an option in configuration.yaml to be passed to pynetgear?


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.114.3
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): N/A
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): MacOS
- Integration causing this issue: netgear
- Link to integration documentation on our website: [https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/netgear](url)

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```yaml
device_tracker:
  - platform: netgear
    password: !secret netgear
    port: 80
    new_device_defaults:
      track_new_devices: false
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
Unauthorized response, let's login and retry...
Invalid response
Get attached devices failed
Error communicating with the Netgear router
```

## Additional information
As a workaround I edited pynetgear/__init__.py to use force_login_v2=True as default.

We no longer accept YAML configuration for integrations that connect to devices or services.

Instead, a configuration flow via the UI should be used.

For more information about this decision see:

- ADR-0007: <https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0007-integration-config-yaml-structure.md#decision>
- ADR-0010: <https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0010-integration-configuration.md#decision>

To get started on the integration configuration, see our developer documentation:

<https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/config_entries_config_flow_handler>
Sounds good. May take me longer to implement. Shall I update this PR or create new with expanded scope?
Either is fine, depends a bit on how long you think it takes to implement. If you think weeks or longer, it might be a good idea to close it for now and re-open when ready.
See https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/34779 for an open PR that adds config flow to netgear.
Is that moving along okay? Should I work independently towards config flow? Wait for #34779 then add V2 login? Merge this ahead of #34779? I'm open to whatever.
Aks the other PR author if you can join forces and finish that PR. We won't merge this PR until there is a config flow in place.
